g.text: HostTCD TX: large parents, buffered chunks, fixed sample timeline

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(245, 247, 250), rgb(24, 25, 28)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(168, 185, 199), rgb(68, 83, 95));

g.text: 1. Split the parent in host memory
Parent: source address per channel, payload length, format, first-sample timestamp T
Shown for channel c; the same chunk index applies to every participating channel.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(219, 230, 240), rgb(32, 42, 50)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(35, 68, 93), rgb(160, 188, 210));

g.text: S = split_size in bytes/channel; N = samples/chunk; chunk i starts at T + i × N.
N = 4096: S = 12288 bytes for IQ12 or 16384 bytes for IQ16. Timestamp spacing is identical.

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(35, 68, 93), rgb(160, 188, 210)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(35, 68, 93), rgb(160, 188, 210));

g.text: 2. Prefetch and play through three buffers per channel

g.text: Buffers exchange roles after release. Issued DMA responses must drain before a buffer can be reused.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(245, 247, 250), rgb(24, 25, 28)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(168, 185, 199), rgb(68, 83, 95));

g.text: 3. Recover from a late chunk without moving the timeline
Example: chunk 0 played; chunk 1 misses its start. Chunk 3 is the earliest with enough preparation time.

g.text: Select earliest chunk with scheduled tick ≥ current tick + preparation budget.
Recheck readiness at its tick; skip again if needed. If no chunk qualifies, discard the remaining parent.
The gap remains at its original sample positions. All channels advance together.
